113def _should_emit_as_log(line: str) -> bool: 

114 """Whether a daemon output line belongs in the general log viewer. 

115 

116 Voice feedback protocol is routed to the face rather than displayed as 

117 a log line. Chat IPC is carved out. Its ``complete`` event carries the whole 

118 assistant reply, which can echo back whatever the user typed, and the 

119 log window is not covered by the redaction invariant the chat path 

120 maintains. Diary IPC stays: it carries progress and token deltas the 

121 log window exists to show. 

122 """ 

123 from jarvis.daemon import CHAT_IPC_PREFIX, VOICE_IPC_PREFIX 

124 

125 return not line.startswith((CHAT_IPC_PREFIX, VOICE_IPC_PREFIX))

243def _format_runtime_status(snapshot: RuntimeStatusSnapshot) -> str: 

244 """Format a runtime status snapshot for the tray diagnostics dialog.""" 

245 lines: list[str] = ["🩺 Runtime Status", ""] 

246 current_section = None 

247 for section, key, value in _runtime_status_rows(snapshot): 

248 if section != current_section: 

249 if current_section is not None: 

250 lines.append("") 

251 lines.append(section) 

252 current_section = section 

253 lines.append(f" {key}: {value}") 

254 return "\n".join(lines)

371 elif process is not None: 371 ↛ 384line 371 didn't jump to line 384 because the condition on line 371 was always true

390def _trim_extension_modules(logs: str) -> str: 

391 """Shorten the faulthandler 'Extension modules:' line to a brief summary. 

392 

393 This line typically consumes 1500-2500 chars of module names that rarely 

394 help with crash diagnosis. Replacing it frees space for the critical 

395 'Fatal Python error' header and current-thread stack trace. 

396 """ 

397 import re 

398 # Match "Extension modules: mod1, mod2, ... (total: N)\n" 

399 m = re.search( 

400 r'^(Extension modules:) [^\n]+\(total: (\d+)\)\s*$', 

401 logs, re.MULTILINE, 

402 ) 

403 if m: 

404 return logs[:m.start()] + f"{m.group(1)} ({m.group(2)} total — trimmed for brevity)\n" + logs[m.end():] 

405 

406 # Fallback: line without "(total: N)" — just truncate after first few modules 

407 m = re.search( 

408 r'^(Extension modules:) (.{80}).+$', 

409 logs, re.MULTILINE, 

410 ) 

411 if m: 411 ↛ 414line 411 didn't jump to line 414 because the condition on line 411 was always true

412 return logs[:m.start()] + f"{m.group(1)} {m.group(2)}... (trimmed)\n" + logs[m.end():] 

413 

414 return logs 

415

417def _extract_fatal_section(logs: str) -> str: 

418 """Extract the 'Fatal Python error' header + current thread stack. 

419 

420 In faulthandler dumps these lines carry the actual crash cause and 

421 appear between the fatal error line and the first other thread 

422 (i.e. the first ``Thread 0x`` header after ``Current thread 0x``). 

423 Returns "" if not found. 

424 """ 

425 import re 

426 # Find "Fatal Python error: ..." line 

427 m = re.search(r'^Fatal Python error: .+$', logs, re.MULTILINE) 

428 if not m: 

429 return "" 

430 

431 start = m.start() 

432 

433 # Grab everything up to (but not including) the first "Thread 0x" header. 

434 # "Current thread 0x..." uses a different prefix so won't match here. 

435 rest = logs[start:] 

436 first_other_thread = next(re.finditer(r'^Thread 0x', rest, re.MULTILINE), None) 

437 if first_other_thread: 

438 end = start + first_other_thread.start() 

439 else: 

440 # No other thread header — take up to 500 chars 

441 end = start + min(500, len(rest)) 

442 

443 return logs[start:end].rstrip() + "\n" 

444 

445 

446def _snap_to_line_boundary(text: str) -> str: 

447 """Advance past a partial first line so truncated output starts cleanly.""" 

448 newline_idx = text.find('\n') 

449 if newline_idx != -1 and newline_idx < 200: 449 ↛ 451line 449 didn't jump to line 451 because the condition on line 449 was always true

450 return text[newline_idx + 1:] 

451 return text

454def _truncate_logs_for_report(logs: str, max_len: int) -> str: 

455 """Truncate logs keeping init section + recent tail. 

456 

457 Recent logs are more valuable for debugging, so we preserve the tail. 

458 The init section (everything up to the last separator line) is kept 

459 for context (version, platform, configuration info). 

460 

461 For faulthandler crash dumps, the bulky 'Extension modules:' line is 

462 trimmed first and the 'Fatal Python error' header + current thread 

463 stack are preserved as a priority section so the root cause survives 

464 truncation. 

465 """ 

466 # Trim the Extension modules line before size check — it wastes ~1700 

467 # chars of budget on module names that almost never help diagnose a crash. 

468 if "Extension modules:" in logs: 

469 logs = _trim_extension_modules(logs) 

470 

471 if len(logs) <= max_len: 

472 return logs 

473 

474 marker = "\n\n... (truncated) ...\n\n" 

475 

476 # Find the init section: everything up to and including the last separator line 

477 last_sep = logs.rfind(_LOG_SEPARATOR) 

478 if last_sep != -1: 

479 init_end = logs.find('\n', last_sep) 

480 if init_end == -1: 480 ↛ 481line 480 didn't jump to line 481 because the condition on line 480 was never true

481 init_end = last_sep + len(_LOG_SEPARATOR) 

482 else: 

483 init_end += 1 # Include the newline 

484 init_section = logs[:init_end] 

485 else: 

486 # No separator found (e.g. crash logs); skip init preservation 

487 init_section = "" 

488 

489 # For faulthandler dumps, extract the fatal error + current thread stack 

490 # as a second must-keep section (the most diagnostic part of the dump). 

491 fatal_section = _extract_fatal_section(logs) 

492 

493 # Cap fatal_section so it never alone exceeds the budget 

494 fatal_cap = max(0, max_len - len(marker) - 200) # leave room for tail 

495 if len(fatal_section) > fatal_cap: 

496 fatal_section = fatal_section[:fatal_cap].rstrip() + "\n" 

497 

498 if len(init_section) + len(fatal_section) + len(marker) * 2 >= max_len: 498 ↛ 500line 498 didn't jump to line 500 because the condition on line 498 was never true

499 # Budget too tight — keep fatal section + tail only 

500 if fatal_section: 

501 tail_budget = max(0, max_len - len(fatal_section) - len(marker)) 

502 if tail_budget == 0: 

503 return fatal_section[:max_len] 

504 tail_part = _snap_to_line_boundary(logs[-tail_budget:]) 

505 return fatal_section + marker + tail_part 

506 

507 # No fatal section — just keep the tail 

508 tail_budget = max(0, max_len - len(marker)) 

509 tail_part = _snap_to_line_boundary(logs[-tail_budget:]) 

510 return marker.lstrip() + tail_part 

511 

512 # Build: init_section + marker + fatal_section + marker + tail 

513 fixed_parts = init_section + marker + fatal_section 

514 if fatal_section: 

515 fixed_parts += marker 

516 

517 tail_budget = max(0, max_len - len(fixed_parts)) 

518 tail_part = _snap_to_line_boundary(logs[-tail_budget:]) 

519 

520 return fixed_parts + tail_part

523def setup_crash_logging(): 

524 """Set up crash logging for the bundled app to capture startup errors.""" 

525 if getattr(sys, 'frozen', False): 

526 # Running as bundled app - use shared crash path helper 

527 crash_log, _, _ = get_crash_paths() 

528 log_file = crash_log 

529 log_dir = log_file.parent 

530 

531 try: 

532 log_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) 

533 

534 # Redirect stdout and stderr to log file with line buffering for immediate writes 

535 # buffering=1 means line-buffered mode (flush on newline) 

536 log_handle = open(log_file, 'w', encoding='utf-8', buffering=1) 

537 sys.stdout = log_handle 

538 sys.stderr = log_handle 

539 

540 # Enable faulthandler to dump Python traceback on segfaults/aborts 

541 # This catches SIGSEGV, SIGFPE, SIGABRT, SIGBUS, SIGILL 

542 import faulthandler 

543 faulthandler.enable(file=log_handle) 

544 

545 print(f"=== Jarvis Desktop App Crash Log ===", flush=True) 

546 print(f"Timestamp: {__import__('datetime').datetime.now()}", flush=True) 

547 print(f"Platform: {sys.platform}", flush=True) 

548 print(f"Python: {sys.version}", flush=True) 

549 print(f"Executable: {sys.executable}", flush=True) 

550 print(f"Frozen: {getattr(sys, 'frozen', False)}", flush=True) 

551 print(f"Bundle dir: {getattr(sys, '_MEIPASS', 'N/A')}", flush=True) 

552 print("=" * 50, flush=True) 

553 print(f"📁 This log: {log_file}", flush=True) 

554 if sys.platform == "darwin": 

555 print(f"📁 System crash reports: ~/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports/", flush=True) 

556 elif sys.platform == "win32": 

557 print(f"📁 Windows Event Viewer: eventvwr.msc → Windows Logs → Application", flush=True) 

558 print("=" * 50, flush=True) 

559 print(flush=True) 

560 

561 return log_file 

562 except Exception as e: 

563 # If we can't set up logging, at least try to show a dialog 

564 return None 

565 return None

588 "Fatal Python error: Aborted" crashes are C-level aborts whose native 

589 stack faulthandler cannot capture (it only dumps Python frames). The 

590 OS still writes a full report to ``~/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports/``; 

591 surfacing its exception type and top native frames alongside the Python 

592 dump makes these crashes diagnosable (#584/#575/#576). 

593 

594 Returns a short human-readable excerpt (exception type, termination 

595 indicator, process name and the top native frames of the crashed 

596 thread), or ``None`` when no report applies: non-macOS platform, 

597 missing/empty diagnostics directory, no report newer than the crash 

598 log, or unparseable content. 

599 """ 

600 if sys.platform != "darwin": 

601 return None 

602 try: 

603 if diagnostics_dir is None: 603 ↛ 604line 603 didn't jump to line 604 because the condition on line 603 was never true

604 diagnostics_dir = Path.home() / "Library" / "Logs" / "DiagnosticReports" 

605 if not diagnostics_dir.is_dir(): 605 ↛ 606line 605 didn't jump to line 606 because the condition on line 605 was never true

606 return None 

607 

608 app_name = "Jarvis" 

609 since = crash_log_path.stat().st_mtime if crash_log_path.exists() else 0.0 

610 

611 candidates = [] 

612 for report in diagnostics_dir.glob(f"{app_name}-*.ips"): 

613 try: 

614 if report.stat().st_mtime >= since: 614 ↛ 612line 614 didn't jump to line 612 because the condition on line 614 was always true

615 candidates.append(report) 

616 except OSError: 

617 continue 

618 if not candidates: 618 ↛ 619line 618 didn't jump to line 619 because the condition on line 618 was never true

619 return None 

620 newest = max(candidates, key=lambda p: p.stat().st_mtime) 

621 

622 raw_text = newest.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") 

623 # .ips files are usually two lines (metadata dict, then the JSON 

624 # payload), but the payload can also span multiple lines when the 

625 # system pretty-prints it. Try the whole file, then everything after 

626 # the first (metadata) line, then the last line alone. 

627 import json as _json 

628 lines = raw_text.splitlines() 

629 candidates = [raw_text] 

630 if lines: 630 ↛ 633line 630 didn't jump to line 633 because the condition on line 630 was always true

631 candidates.append("\n".join(lines[1:])) 

632 candidates.append(lines[-1]) 

633 data = None 

634 for candidate in candidates: 634 ↛ 643line 634 didn't jump to line 643 because the loop on line 634 didn't complete

635 stripped = candidate.strip() 

636 if not stripped.startswith("{"): 636 ↛ 637line 636 didn't jump to line 637 because the condition on line 636 was never true

637 continue 

638 try: 

639 data = _json.loads(stripped) 

640 break 

641 except Exception: 

642 continue 

643 if not isinstance(data, dict): 643 ↛ 644line 643 didn't jump to line 644 because the condition on line 643 was never true

644 return None 

645 

646 parts = [f"🧵 Native crash report: {newest.name}"] 

647 exc = data.get("exception") or {} 

648 if exc.get("type"): 648 ↛ 650line 648 didn't jump to line 650 because the condition on line 648 was always true

649 parts.append(f" Exception: {exc['type']}") 

650 term = data.get("termination") or {} 

651 if term.get("indicator"): 651 ↛ 654line 651 didn't jump to line 654 because the condition on line 651 was always true

652 parts.append(f" Termination: {term['indicator']}") 

653 

654 crashed = None 

655 for thread in data.get("threads") or []: 655 ↛ 659line 655 didn't jump to line 659 because the loop on line 655 didn't complete

656 if thread.get("triggered"): 

657 crashed = thread 

658 break 

659 if crashed is None and data.get("threads"): 659 ↛ 660line 659 didn't jump to line 660 because the condition on line 659 was never true

660 crashed = data["threads"][0] 

661 frames = (crashed or {}).get("frames") or [] 

662 if frames: 662 ↛ 671line 662 didn't jump to line 671 because the condition on line 662 was always true

663 parts.append(" Native frames (crashed thread):") 

664 for frame in frames[:max_frames]: 

665 # ``symbol`` is the demangled name; ``symbolLocation`` is a 

666 # byte offset — never fall back to it for display. 

667 symbol = frame.get("symbol") 

668 if not isinstance(symbol, str) or not symbol: 668 ↛ 669line 668 didn't jump to line 669 because the condition on line 668 was never true

669 symbol = "?" 

670 parts.append(f" {symbol}") 

671 return "\n".join(parts) 

672 except Exception: 

673 return None

676def check_previous_crash() -> Optional[str]: 

677 """ 

678 Check if previous session crashed and return crash details if so. 

679 

680 Returns crash log content if previous session crashed, None otherwise. 

681 """ 

682 try: 

683 crash_log, crash_marker, previous_crash = get_crash_paths() 

684 

685 if crash_marker.exists(): 

686 # Previous session didn't exit cleanly 

687 crash_marker.unlink() 

688 

689 crash_content = None 

690 

691 # Check for crash log content 

692 if crash_log.exists(): 

693 content = crash_log.read_text(encoding='utf-8', errors='replace') 

694 # Only report if there's actual crash info (faulthandler output or errors) 

695 if 'Fatal' in content or 'Error' in content or 'Traceback' in content: 

696 crash_content = content 

697 # On macOS, append the native .ips stack so the crash 

698 # dialog and report-issue body carry the C-level abort 

699 # source faulthandler cannot show. 

700 native = collect_macos_crash_report(crash_log) 

701 if native: 

702 crash_content += f"\n{native}\n" 

703 # Save to previous_crash for reference 

704 previous_crash.write_text(crash_content, encoding='utf-8') 

705 

706 return crash_content 

707 

708 return None 

709 except Exception: 

710 return None

1021 """Get the path to the single-instance lock file.""" 

1022 if sys.platform == "darwin": 

1023 lock_dir = Path.home() / "Library" / "Application Support" / "Jarvis" 

1024 elif sys.platform == "win32":

1026 else:

1030 return lock_dir / "jarvis_desktop.lock"

1046def kill_existing_instance(pid: int) -> bool: 

1047 """ 

1048 Terminate an existing Jarvis instance by PID. 

1049 

1050 Returns True if the process was terminated, False otherwise. 

1051 """ 

1052 try: 

1053 process = psutil.Process(pid) 

1054 # Verify it's actually a Jarvis process (safety check) 

1055 proc_name = process.name().lower() 

1056 if "jarvis" not in proc_name and "python" not in proc_name: 

1057 debug_log(f"PID {pid} doesn't look like Jarvis (name: {proc_name}), not killing", "desktop") 

1058 return False 

1059 

1060 debug_log(f"Terminating existing Jarvis instance (PID {pid})", "desktop") 

1061 process.terminate() 

1062 

1063 # Wait up to 5 seconds for graceful shutdown 

1064 try: 

1065 process.wait(timeout=5) 

1066 except psutil.TimeoutExpired: 

1067 debug_log(f"Process {pid} didn't terminate gracefully, force killing", "desktop") 

1068 process.kill() 

1069 process.wait(timeout=2) 

1070 

1071 return True 

1072 except psutil.NoSuchProcess: 

1073 # Process already gone 

1074 return True 

1075 except Exception as e: 

1076 debug_log(f"Failed to kill process {pid}: {e}", "desktop") 

1077 return False

1110def acquire_single_instance_lock() -> bool: 

1111 """ 

1112 Acquire a lock to ensure only one instance of the desktop app runs. 

1113 

1114 Returns True if lock acquired (we're the only instance), False otherwise. 

1115 The lock file handle is kept open globally to maintain the lock. 

1116 """ 

1117 global _lock_file_handle 

1118 

1119 lock_file = get_lock_file_path() 

1120 

1121 try: 

1122 # Open in append+read binary mode — does NOT truncate the file. 

1123 # Opening with 'w' would truncate immediately, destroying the existing 

1124 # instance's PID before we even attempt the lock, making it unreadable. 

1125 _lock_file_handle = open(lock_file, 'a+b') 

1126 

1127 if sys.platform == "win32": 1127 ↛ 1132line 1127 didn't jump to line 1132 because the condition on line 1127 was never true

1128 # Windows: use msvcrt for file locking. 

1129 # Lock at _LOCK_OFFSET (not byte 0) so the PID content at bytes 

1130 # 0–~10 remains readable by other processes. msvcrt.locking() 

1131 # creates mandatory locks that block ALL I/O on the locked bytes. 

1132 import msvcrt 

1133 _lock_file_handle.seek(_LOCK_OFFSET) 

1134 try: 

1135 msvcrt.locking(_lock_file_handle.fileno(), msvcrt.LK_NBLCK, 1) 

1136 except OSError: 

1137 # Lock failed — another instance is running 

1138 _lock_file_handle.close() 

1139 _lock_file_handle = None 

1140 return False 

1141 else: 

1142 # Unix (macOS, Linux): use fcntl for file locking 

1143 import fcntl 

1144 try: 

1145 fcntl.flock(_lock_file_handle.fileno(), fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB) 

1146 except (IOError, OSError): 

1147 # Lock failed - another instance is running 

1148 _lock_file_handle.close() 

1149 _lock_file_handle = None 

1150 return False 

1151 

1152 # Lock acquired — overwrite the file with our PID 

1153 _lock_file_handle.seek(0) 

1154 _lock_file_handle.truncate(0) 

1155 _lock_file_handle.write(str(os.getpid()).encode()) 

1156 _lock_file_handle.flush() 

1157 

1158 # Register cleanup to release lock on exit 

1159 def release_lock(): 

1160 global _lock_file_handle 

1161 if _lock_file_handle: 

1162 try: 

1163 _lock_file_handle.close() 

1164 except Exception: 

1165 pass 

1166 _lock_file_handle = None 

1167 

1168 atexit.register(release_lock) 

1169 

1170 return True 

1171 

1172 except Exception as e: 

1173 print(f"Warning: Could not acquire single-instance lock: {e}") 

1174 # On any error, allow the app to run (fail open) 

1175 return True 

1176

1304 def append_log(self, text: str) -> None: 

1305 """Keep transfer updates in a card and important events in the timeline.""" 

1306 for line in clean_log(text).replace('\r', '\n').splitlines(): 

1307 if not line.strip(): 

1308 continue 

1309 progress = parse_progress(line) 

1310 if progress: 

1311 previous = self._downloads.get(progress.name) 

1312 self._downloads[progress.name] = progress 

1313 self._download_times[progress.name] = time.monotonic() 

1314 if progress.percent == 100: 

1315 if previous is None or previous.percent != 100: 

1316 self._append_event(f"✅ Downloaded {progress.name} · {progress.detail}") 

1317 # A small metadata file can finish while model weights are 

1318 # still transferring on another Hub worker. 

1319 progress = next((p for p in self._downloads.values() if p.percent != 100), progress) 

1320 elif previous is None or previous.percent == 100: 

1321 self._append_event(f"📥 Downloading {progress.name}") 

1322 self.download_card.show() 

1323 self.download_title.setText(f"📥 {progress.name}") 

1324 self.download_bar.setFormat('%p%') 

1325 self.download_bar.setRange(0, 0 if progress.percent is None else 100) 

1326 if progress.percent is not None: 

1327 self.download_bar.setValue(progress.percent) 

1328 self._progress_detail = progress.detail 

1329 self.download_detail.setText(progress.detail) 

1330 self._last_progress_at = self._download_times[progress.name] 

1331 if progress.percent != 100: 

1332 self._progress_timer.start() 

1333 else: 

1334 self._progress_timer.stop() 

1335 self.download_card.hide() 

1336 continue 

1337 if line.startswith('📥 Checking Whisper model files'): 

1338 self._downloads.clear() 

1339 self._download_times.clear() 

1340 self.download_card.show() 

1341 self.download_title.setText('📥 Preparing Whisper model files') 

1342 self.download_bar.setRange(0, 0) 

1343 self.download_bar.setFormat('%p%') 

1344 self._progress_detail = 'Checking the local cache and model server' 

1345 self.download_detail.setText(self._progress_detail) 

1346 self._last_progress_at = time.monotonic() 

1347 self._progress_timer.start() 

1348 elif line.startswith('🎤 Loading Whisper into memory'): 

1349 self._progress_timer.stop() 

1350 self.download_card.show() 

1351 self.download_title.setText('🎤 Preparing speech recognition') 

1352 self.download_bar.setFormat('%p%') 

1353 self.download_bar.setRange(0, 0) 

1354 self._progress_detail = 'Model files ready · loading into memory and warming up' 

1355 self.download_detail.setText(self._progress_detail) 

1356 elif ('MLX Whisper' in line and 'ready (Apple Silicon GPU)' in line 

1357 or line.strip() == '🎙️ Listening! Try:'): 

1358 self._progress_timer.stop() 

1359 self.download_card.hide() 

1360 if any(message in line for message in ( 

1361 'Download failed', 'Download error', 'Failed to initialise MLX Whisper', 

1362 'Daemon exited unexpectedly', 'Daemon stopped', 

1363 )): 

1364 self._progress_timer.stop() 

1365 self._downloads.clear() 

1366 self._download_times.clear() 

1367 if not self.download_card.isHidden(): 1367 ↛ 1371line 1367 didn't jump to line 1371 because the condition on line 1367 was always true

1368 self.download_bar.setRange(0, 100) 

1369 self.download_bar.setFormat('Interrupted') 

1370 self.download_detail.setText(self._progress_detail + " · See details below") 

1371 self._append_event(line)

1373 def _append_event(self, line): 

1374 cursor = self.log_display.textCursor() 

1375 cursor.movePosition(QTextCursor.MoveOperation.End) 

1376 style = QTextCharFormat() 

1377 style.setForeground(QColor(COLORS['text_muted'])) 

1378 cursor.insertText(time.strftime('%H:%M:%S') + ' ', style) 

1379 colour = 'text_primary' 

1380 if '❌' in line or 'Traceback' in line: 

1381 colour = 'error_light' 

1382 elif '⚠' in line: 

1383 colour = 'warning_light' 

1384 elif line.lstrip().startswith(('✓', '✅')): 

1385 colour = 'success_light' 

1386 style.setForeground(QColor(COLORS[colour])) 

1387 cursor.insertText(line + '\n', style) 

1388 self.log_display.setTextCursor(cursor) 

1389 self.log_display.ensureCursorVisible()

1394 self.download_detail.setText(

1552 """Start the memory viewer Flask server."""

1555 return True 

1556

1558 

1559 try: 

1560 # Check if server is already running on the port 

1561 import socket 

1562 sock = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM) 

1563 result = sock.connect_ex(('localhost', self.MEMORY_VIEWER_PORT)) 

1564 sock.close() 

1565 

1566 if result == 0: 

1567 # Port is already in use, assume server is running 

1568 self.is_server_running = True

1577 if is_frozen:

1590

1595 debug=False, 

1596 use_reloader=False, 

1597 threaded=True 

1598 ) 

1599 except Exception as server_err: 

1600 debug_log(f"memory viewer server error: {server_err}", "desktop") 

1601 

1602 self.server_thread = threading.Thread(target=run_flask_server, daemon=True)

1605 

1606 # For bundled mode, use simple wait - Flask thread starts quickly 

1607 # The complex socket polling below is for subprocess mode reliability 

1608 import time 

1609 time.sleep(1) 

1610 self.is_server_running = True 

1611 return True 

1612 else: 

1613 # Development: start server in subprocess

1617 env = os.environ.copy() 

1618 src_path = Path(__file__).parent.parent # Go up to src/ 

1619 if "PYTHONPATH" in env: 

1620 env["PYTHONPATH"] = f"{src_path}{os.pathsep}{env['PYTHONPATH']}" 

1621 else: 

1622 env["PYTHONPATH"] = str(src_path) 

1623 

1624 # Ensure UTF-8 encoding for subprocess (Windows cp1252 can't handle emojis) 

1625 env["PYTHONIOENCODING"] = "utf-8" 

1626 

1627 # Use creationflags to prevent console window popup on Windows 

1628 creationflags = 0 

1629 if sys.platform == 'win32': 

1630 creationflags = subprocess.CREATE_NO_WINDOW 

1631 

1632 print(f" -> Python: {python_exe}", flush=True) 

1633 print(f" -> PYTHONPATH: {env.get('PYTHONPATH', 'not set')}", flush=True) 

1634 

1635 self.server_process = subprocess.Popen( 

1636 [python_exe, "-m", "desktop_app.memory_viewer"],

1652 max_wait = 5 # seconds 

1653 start_time = time.time() 

1654

1710 def stop_server(self) -> None: 

1711 """Stop the memory viewer Flask server.""" 

1712 if self.server_process: 

1713 try: 

1714 self.server_process.terminate() 

1715 self.server_process.wait(timeout=3) 

1716 except subprocess.TimeoutExpired: 

1717 self.server_process.kill() 

1718 self.server_process.wait() 

1719 except Exception as e: 

1720 debug_log(f"error stopping memory viewer server: {e}", "desktop") 

1721 finally: 

1722 self.server_process = None 

1723 self.is_server_running = False 

1724 

1725 # Thread-based server (bundled mode) will stop when app exits (daemon thread) 

1726 if self.server_thread: 

1727 self.server_thread = None 

1728 self.is_server_running = False

1785class DaemonThread(KeepAliveWorker): 

1786 """QThread that runs the Jarvis daemon inside the bundled app. 

1787 

1788 Inherits ``KeepAliveWorker`` so the object stays referenced in the 

1789 registry until its OS thread has fully finished: ``_on_daemon_finished`` 

1790 clears ``tray.daemon_thread`` from a ``finished``-connected slot, and 

1791 dropping that last reference while the thread is still winding down 

1792 would destroy a running QThread and abort the whole app ("Fatal Python 

1793 error: Aborted" — #584/#575/#576, same class as #509/#407/#239). 

1794 """ 

1795 

1796 def __init__(self, log_signals): 

1797 super().__init__() 

1798 self.log_signals = log_signals 

1799 

1800 def run(self): 

1801 """Run the daemon in this QThread.""" 

1802 import sys as sys_module 

1803 old_stdout = sys_module.stdout 

1804 old_stderr = sys_module.stderr 

1805 feedback_setter = None 

1806 

1807 try: 

1808 # Redirect stdout/stderr to capture logs 

1809 log_writer = LogStream(self.log_signals.new_log.emit) 

1810 sys_module.stdout = log_writer 

1811 sys_module.stderr = log_writer 

1812 

1813 try: 

1814 # Import and run the daemon 

1815 from jarvis.daemon import main as daemon_main, set_voice_feedback_callback 

1816 feedback_setter = set_voice_feedback_callback 

1817 feedback_setter(self.log_signals.low_confidence.emit) 

1818 self.log_signals.new_log.emit("🚀 Jarvis daemon started\n") 

1819 self.log_signals.new_log.emit("📋 Initializing daemon components...\n") 

1820 

1821 # Run daemon - this should run the main loop 

1822 daemon_main() 

1823 

1824 from jarvis.daemon import is_stop_requested 

1825 if is_stop_requested(): 

1826 self.log_signals.new_log.emit("✅ Daemon stopped gracefully\n") 

1827 else: 

1828 self.log_signals.new_log.emit("⚠️ Daemon exited unexpectedly\n") 

1829 except KeyboardInterrupt: 

1830 self.log_signals.new_log.emit("⏸️ Daemon interrupted\n") 

1831 except Exception as e: 

1832 error_msg = f"❌ Daemon runtime error: {str(e)}\n{traceback.format_exc()}\n" 

1833 self.log_signals.new_log.emit(error_msg) 

1834 # Also try to log via debug_log (though it might not work) 

1835 try: 

1836 debug_log(f"daemon thread error: {e}", "desktop") 

1837 except Exception: 

1838 pass 

1839 finally: 

1840 if feedback_setter is not None: 

1841 feedback_setter(None) 

1842 sys_module.stdout = old_stdout 

1843 sys_module.stderr = old_stderr 

1844 except Exception as e: 

1845 # Outer exception handler for setup errors 

1846 error_msg = f"❌ Daemon setup error: {str(e)}\n{traceback.format_exc()}\n" 

1847 try: 

1848 self.log_signals.new_log.emit(error_msg) 

1849 except Exception: 

1850 # If we can't emit, at least try stdout 

1851 print(error_msg, file=old_stderr) 

1852 

1853

1953 def cleanup_orphaned_processes(self) -> None: 

1954 """Kill any orphaned Jarvis daemon processes from previous sessions.""" 

1955 try: 

1956 current_pid = os.getpid() 

1957 for proc in psutil.process_iter(['pid', 'name', 'cmdline']): 

1958 try: 

1959 cmdline = proc.info.get('cmdline', []) 

1960 if cmdline and 'jarvis.main' in ' '.join(cmdline): 

1961 # This is a Jarvis daemon process 

1962 if proc.pid != current_pid: 

1963 debug_log(f"killing orphaned jarvis process: {proc.pid}", "desktop") 

1964 proc.terminate() 

1965 try: 

1966 proc.wait(timeout=2) 

1967 except psutil.TimeoutExpired: 

1968 proc.kill() 

1969 except (psutil.NoSuchProcess, psutil.AccessDenied): 

1970 continue 

1971 except Exception as e: 

1972 debug_log(f"error cleaning up orphaned processes: {e}", "desktop") 

1973 

1974 def cleanup_on_exit(self) -> None: 

1975 """Cleanup when app is exiting.""" 

1976 debug_log("cleaning up on exit", "desktop") 

1977 if self.is_listening: 1977 ↛ 1978line 1977 didn't jump to line 1978 because the condition on line 1977 was never true

1978 self.stop_daemon() 

1979 # Stop memory viewer server 

1980 if hasattr(self, 'memory_viewer'): 1980 ↛ 1984line 1980 didn't jump to line 1984 because the condition on line 1980 was always true

1981 self.memory_viewer.stop_server() 

1982 # Safety net: if daemon process exists but is_listening was False, still clean up 

1983 # (This shouldn't happen in normal operation, but handles edge cases) 

1984 if self.daemon_process: 1984 ↛ 1985line 1984 didn't jump to line 1985 because the condition on line 1984 was never true

1985 try: 

1986 self.daemon_process.terminate() 

1987 try: 

1988 # Use longer timeout to allow diary update to complete 

1989 self.daemon_process.wait(timeout=60) 

1990 except subprocess.TimeoutExpired: 

1991 self.daemon_process.kill() 

1992 self.daemon_process.wait() 

1993 except Exception as e: 

1994 debug_log(f"error during exit cleanup: {e}", "desktop") 

1995 _stop_owned_ollama_runtime(self._ollama_runtime_ownership) 

1996

2095 else:

2102 self.cuda_recovery_action = QAction(action_spec.label)

2108 def _run_cuda_recovery(self, action_spec: "CudaRecoveryAction") -> None: 

2109 """Confirm with the user, then launch the recovery script with UAC.""" 

2110 from desktop_app.cuda_recovery import run_action 

2111 from PyQt6.QtWidgets import QMessageBox 

2112 

2113 reply = QMessageBox.question( 

2114 None, 

2115 "Reinstall GPU libraries", 

2116 ( 

2117 "This will download cuBLAS and cuDNN (~1.1 GB) and install them " 

2118 "into the Jarvis program folder. You'll see a UAC prompt. " 

2119 "Continue?" 

2120 ), 

2121 QMessageBox.StandardButton.Yes | QMessageBox.StandardButton.No, 

2122 QMessageBox.StandardButton.No, 

2123 ) 

2124 if reply != QMessageBox.StandardButton.Yes: 

2125 return 

2126 

2127 ok = run_action(action_spec) 

2128 if not ok: 

2129 QMessageBox.warning( 

2130 None, 

2131 "Reinstall GPU libraries", 

2132 ( 

2133 "Could not launch the installer. If you dismissed the UAC " 

2134 f"prompt, try again. See the log at\n{action_spec.target_dir / 'install.log'}" 

2135 ), 

2136 ) 

2137 return 

2138 

2139 QMessageBox.information( 

2140 None, 

2141 "Reinstall GPU libraries", 

2142 ( 

2143 "The CUDA installer is running. Once it finishes, restart " 

2144 f"Jarvis to use GPU acceleration. See {action_spec.target_dir / 'install.log'} " 

2145 "for details." 

2146 ), 

2147 )

2194 def collect_runtime_status(self) -> RuntimeStatusSnapshot: 

2195 """Collect current runtime state for the tray diagnostics dialog."""

2204 def show_runtime_status(self) -> None: 

2205 """Show a compact diagnostic summary of Jarvis' active runtime. 

2206 

2207 The snapshot is collected on a worker thread and delivered back 

2208 through a signal, the same marshalling this app already uses for 

2209 chat events. Collecting it inline would run ``check_ollama_server`` 

2210 — a blocking request with a five second timeout — on the Qt main 

2211 thread, freezing every menu in the app at precisely the moment the 

2212 user reached for diagnostics because something looked wrong. 

2213 """ 

2214 import threading 

2215 

2216 def _collect(): 

2217 try: 

2218 snapshot = self.collect_runtime_status() 

2219 except Exception as exc: 

2220 debug_log(f"runtime status collection failed: {exc}", "desktop") 

2221 return 

2222 self._runtime_status_signals.ready.emit(snapshot) 

2223 

2224 threading.Thread( 

2225 target=_collect, name="runtime-status", daemon=True, 

2226 ).start() 

2227 

2228 def _show_runtime_status_dialog(self, snapshot) -> None: 

2229 """Render the collected snapshot. Runs on the Qt main thread.""" 

2230 RuntimeStatusDialog(snapshot).exec()

2232 def check_for_updates(self, show_no_update_dialog: bool = False) -> None: 

2233 """Check for available updates. 

2234 

2235 Args: 

2236 show_no_update_dialog: If True, shows a dialog even when no update is available. 

2237 """ 

2238 from desktop_app.updater import check_for_updates, is_frozen 

2239 from desktop_app.update_dialog import ( 

2240 UpdateAvailableDialog, 

2241 UpdateProgressDialog, 

2242 show_no_update_dialog as show_no_update, 

2243 show_update_error_dialog, 

2244 ) 

2245 

2246 # Only check for updates if running as bundled app 

2247 if not is_frozen(): 

2248 if show_no_update_dialog: 

2249 from PyQt6.QtWidgets import QMessageBox 

2250 msg = QMessageBox() 

2251 msg.setIcon(QMessageBox.Icon.Information) 

2252 msg.setWindowTitle("Updates") 

2253 msg.setText("Auto-update is only available in the bundled desktop app.") 

2254 msg.setInformativeText("You're running from source. Use git pull to update.") 

2255 msg.setStyleSheet(JARVIS_THEME_STYLESHEET) 

2256 msg.exec() 

2257 return 

2258 

2259 try: 

2260 status = check_for_updates() 

2261 

2262 if status.error: 

2263 debug_log(f"Update check failed: {status.error}", "desktop") 

2264 if show_no_update_dialog: 

2265 show_update_error_dialog(status.error) 

2266 return 

2267 

2268 if status.update_available and status.latest_release: 

2269 # Show update available dialog 

2270 dialog = UpdateAvailableDialog(status) 

2271 if dialog.exec() == QDialog.DialogCode.Accepted: 

2272 # User chose to update - create callback to save diary before install 

2273 def save_session_before_update(): 

2274 """Stop daemon and save diary before update installation.""" 

2275 if self.is_listening: 

2276 debug_log("Saving session before update...", "updater") 

2277 self.stop_daemon(show_diary_dialog=True) 

2278 

2279 progress_dialog = UpdateProgressDialog( 

2280 status.latest_release, 

2281 pre_install_callback=save_session_before_update, 

2282 ) 

2283 progress_dialog.show() 

2284 progress_dialog.start_download() 

2285 

2286 result = progress_dialog.exec() 

2287 if result == QDialog.DialogCode.Accepted: 

2288 # Update successful, exit app (diary already saved via pre_install_callback) 

2289 self.quit_app(skip_diary=True) 

2290 elif show_no_update_dialog: 

2291 show_no_update(status.current_version) 

2292 

2293 except Exception as e: 

2294 debug_log(f"Update check error: {e}", "desktop") 

2295 if show_no_update_dialog: 

2296 show_update_error_dialog(str(e))

3050def _ollama_runtime_flags(cfg) -> tuple[bool, bool]: 

3051 """Decide how much of the Ollama startup flow applies given the active 

3052 providers. 

3053 

3054 Returns ``(ollama_needed, chat_on_ollama)``: 

3055 - ``ollama_needed`` — the local Ollama server must be up because chat 

3056 and/or embeddings run on it. False only for a pure OpenAI-compatible 

3057 setup (both chat and embeddings remote), where there is nothing local 

3058 to start or verify. 

3059 - ``chat_on_ollama`` — the chat model is an Ollama model, so the 

3060 chat-model verification / unsupported-model checks apply. False when 

3061 chat runs on an OpenAI-compatible server (its model name is not in the 

3062 Ollama catalogue and would be wrongly flagged as unsupported). 

3063 """ 

3064 llm_provider = getattr(cfg, "llm_provider", "ollama") or "ollama" 

3065 embed_provider = getattr(cfg, "embedding_provider", "") or llm_provider 

3066 ollama_needed = not ( 

3067 llm_provider == "openai_compatible" and embed_provider == "openai_compatible" 

3068 ) 

3069 chat_on_ollama = llm_provider != "openai_compatible" 

3070 return ollama_needed, chat_on_ollama

3143 # Ensure stdout/stderr use UTF-8. PyInstaller GUI-subsystem executables 

3144 # (console=False) can attach an ANSI-code-page stdout (Windows) or even 

3145 # None when there is no console at all; the daemon prints emoji 

3146 # (✅, ✓, 🧠…), so a non-UTF-8 stream raises UnicodeEncodeError (or 

3147 # AttributeError when stdout is None) and the smoke test exits 1 before 

3148 # ever reaching the daemon. Wrap in UTF-8 when a binary buffer is 

3149 # available and fall back to a sink so prints can never crash the test. 

3150 # Only wrap the real console streams: pytest swaps in its own capture 

3151 # objects that must not be re-wrapped (wrapping them detaches and 

3152 # closes their buffers, corrupting output capture for the process). 

3153 try: 

3154 import io 

3155 for _stream_name in ("stdout", "stderr"): 

3156 _stream = getattr(sys, _stream_name) 

3157 _real = getattr(sys, "__" + _stream_name, None) 

3158 if _stream is None: 3158 ↛ 3159line 3158 didn't jump to line 3159 because the condition on line 3158 was never true

3159 setattr(sys, _stream_name, io.StringIO())

3161 and (getattr(sys, "frozen", False) or _stream is _real) \ 

3162 and hasattr(_stream, "buffer") and hasattr(_stream.buffer, "write"): 

3163 setattr(sys, _stream_name, io.TextIOWrapper( 

3164 _stream.buffer, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")) 

3165 except Exception: 

3166 pass

3211 ``check_done`` so it does not shadow QThread's built-in ``finished``. 

3212 """

3218 # Lazy import: app.py keeps setup_wizard loading deferred past 

3219 # crash-logging setup, so resolve it from the worker thread. 

3220 from desktop_app.setup_wizard import should_show_setup_wizard 

3221 result = should_show_setup_wizard() 

3222 self.check_done.emit(result) 

3223 except Exception as e:

3225 # On error, show wizard to let user fix issues 

3226 self.check_done.emit(True)
